The gate accepted none of my three edits, and all 20 calls and 3 submissions are now used. Cluster 0 is still open, and v5 remains the current version.

Each candidate passed the target test (it cut the cluster's bad mass by about 0.11) but failed at least one other test:

| Version | What it did | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| v6 | Rotated flagged decodes counter-clockwise, so all rescued mass went to one neighbouring mode (steps 10–14) | 3, drift |
| v7 | Pushed each flagged decode a fixed amount toward whichever of the two neighbouring modes was closer | 5, off-distribution actions |
| v8 | Same as v7, starting at step 8 | 4, other bad behaviours, and 5 |

All three were grafts on the `out` layer, triggered by a probe I fitted on `out_act`. The probe caught 85–92% of target decodes and fired on 0.4–2% of the rest.

- **Drift:** my guess is that v6 failed because it piled all ~12% of the rescued mass into one mode. Splitting it in v7 fixed drift, which fits that guess, but the gate doesn't report enough to confirm it.
- **Off-distribution:** my own estimate of this rise for v7 was well under the 0.02 limit, so the gate measures it differently from how I did.
- **v8 was a blind change:** I had no calls left to simulate it or run `quick_check` first.

A next session could try a sharper split so fewer decodes end up stuck between modes; my last sandbox simulation did not test this. The probe and graft arrays (`d_w.npy`, `q_*.npy`, `r_*.npy`, `s_*.npy`) are in `/home/user/preference_toy/runs/repair/a3lf_cond_alt_s8_n4/scratch`.
